issues.description: TTS v3 default_speaker in TTS_MODEL_CONFIGS is 'shubh' but PR description and code comments say 'aditya'
issues.detail: In TTS_MODEL_CONFIGS, the bulbul:v3-beta entry sets default_speaker='shubh', but the PR description, the module docstring ('aditya (default)'), and the class docstring all state the default v3 speaker is 'aditya'. This inconsistency means users relying on documented defaults will get a different voice than expected. Pick one and align all references.

issues.description: STT _connect() removed 'input_audio_codec' but kept self._input_audio_codec read elsewhere, breaking codec negotiation
issues.detail: The new _connect() drops 'input_audio_codec' from connect_kwargs entirely (previously sent). If the Sarvam SDK requires this for non-default codecs, transcription will fail for non-wav inputs. Either restore the kwarg or document/verify the SDK now infers it. The __init__ still accepts input_audio_codec as a parameter, suggesting it was intended to remain functional.

issues.description: Pace clamping warning fires but Pydantic Field validation will reject out-of-range values first
issues.detail: InputParams declares pace with ge=0.3, le=3.0 via Pydantic Field. A user passing pace=2.5 for v3 (range 0.5-2.0) will pass Pydantic validation, but pace=0.4 for v3 will also pass Pydantic. The clamp logic then handles the v3-specific narrower range. However, values like pace=4.0 are rejected by Pydantic before clamping. This is fine, but the clamp warning suggests a more graceful interaction than reality; document that Pydantic still enforces the union of ranges, not the model-specific one.

issues.description: Warnings on default values trigger false positives when user explicitly passes the default
issues.detail: The code checks `params.pitch != 0.0`, `params.loudness != 1.0`, `params.temperature != 0.6` to decide whether to warn about unsupported parameters. But these are also the Pydantic defaults — a user who explicitly passes pitch=0.0 (the default) on v3 won't get a warning, while a user who passes pitch=0.1 will. Conversely, a v2 user accepting defaults will never see warnings, which is fine, but the asymmetry means warnings depend on whether the user typed the default vs. relied on it. Use a sentinel or check `model_fields_set` to detect explicit user input.

issues.description: voice_id is not validated against the model's speaker list
issues.detail: TTSModelConfig.speakers enumerates allowed speakers per model, and get_speakers_for_model() exists as a helper, but __init__ never validates voice_id against self._config.speakers. A v3 user passing voice_id='anushka' (a v2-only voice) will get an opaque API error at runtime instead of a clear ValueError at construction. Add validation: `if voice_id not in self._config.speakers: raise ValueError(...)`.

issues.description: Backward incompatibility: previously-accepted models like 'bulbul:v3' (non-beta) now raise ValueError
issues.detail: The previous TTS __init__ had a branch `if model in ('bulbul:v3-beta', 'bulbul:v3')`, indicating 'bulbul:v3' was accepted. The new strict whitelist only includes 'bulbul:v2' and 'bulbul:v3-beta', so existing user code passing 'bulbul:v3' now fails at construction. Either add an alias or call this out as a breaking change in CHANGELOG.

issues.description: STT __init__ does not enforce mode value against the configured model's allowed modes
issues.detail: InputParams.mode is a Literal of five string values, which Pydantic enforces. But the ValueError 'does not support mode parameter' fires only when supports_mode is False. There is no per-model whitelist of which modes are valid for saaras:v3 specifically — the Literal allows all five for any future model. Acceptable today since only one model supports mode, but worth a TODO if other models will support a subset.

issues.description: set_language() on saaras:v2.5 now raises ValueError where previously it may have been a no-op
issues.detail: Previously set_language() raised only for models with 'saaras' in the name (both v2.5 and v3). The new logic raises whenever `not self._config.supports_language`. For saaras:v3, supports_language=True, so calling set_language() works. For saaras:v2.5 (supports_language=False), it raises. This is consistent with the PR's intent, but the docstring/PR description should make it explicit that v3 now supports set_language() while v2.5 does not.

issues.description: Typo-style inconsistency: docstring example uses 'bulbul:v3' without 'beta' suffix
issues.detail: In the old class docstring example: `model="bulbul:v3,` (also has unclosed quote in original). The new docstring fixes it to 'bulbul:v3-beta'. Verify all example/test code uses the canonical 'bulbul:v3-beta'.

issues.description: get_speakers_for_model falls back to v2 speakers for unknown models, silently masking typos
issues.detail: If a caller passes a misspelled model name, they get v2's speaker list with no error. A KeyError or returning an empty list with a warning would surface bugs faster. Low impact since the helper is informational.

issues.description: Pydantic Field defaults on Optional[float] with ge/le constraints — None is technically not in range
issues.detail: pitch/pace/loudness/temperature are typed Optional[float] but have numeric defaults and ge/le constraints. None would bypass range validation but the defaults are non-None. Consider whether Optional is intentional or if these should be plain float. Cosmetic.

issues.description: Dead/unused import: Enum imported but only used for str-based enums
issues.detail: Three Enum classes are added (SarvamTTSModel, SarvamTTSSpeakerV2, SarvamTTSSpeakerV3), but SarvamTTSModel does not appear to be referenced anywhere in the diff outside its own definition. Confirm it's exported / used by callers; otherwise it's dead code.

dissents.topic: Strict model whitelist vs. permissive fallback

positions.position: Raising ValueError on unknown models is correct — keeps the type surface honest and prevents silent misconfiguration. The previous string-matching ('saaras' in model.lower()) was fragile.
Users in the wild may already be passing 'bulbul:v3' (the old code accepted it). A hard ValueError is a breaking change; an alias or deprecation warning would preserve compatibility.

dissents.topic: Warning vs. raising for unsupported parameters on v3

positions.position: Silently ignoring pitch/loudness on v3 (with only a warning) violates least-surprise. If a user sets pitch, they expect it to take effect or to be told it cannot — raise ValueError like the STT side does.

TTS users frequently swap models without rewriting param objects. Warning + ignore is the friendlier default; raising would force every call site to branch on model. The STT side raises because its parameters are more semantically load-bearing (prompts/language).
PR description and docstrings say 'aditya'; the config sets 'shubh'. The spec is authoritative — fix the config.
Whatever the code actually sets is what ships. Update the docs to match 'shubh' if that's the intended default — but either way, the divergence must be resolved before merge.

review.summary: The PR cleanly refactors Sarvam STT and TTS into table-driven, config-object designs, which is a clear improvement over the previous string-match-on-model-name logic. However, there is a P0 inconsistency between the documented default v3 speaker ('aditya') and the configured default ('shubh'), and a likely-P0 silent removal of 'input_audio_codec' from the STT connect kwargs that may break non-wav callers. Several P1 concerns center on UX: missing voice_id validation against the model's speaker enum, warnings that compare against defaults (so explicit defaults are indistinguishable from implicit ones), and a backward-incompatible drop of the 'bulbul:v3' alias. The STT/TTS sides are also asymmetric in their handling of unsupported parameters (STT raises, TTS warns), which is defensible but worth calling out in the changelog.
